## Summary

deepsec flagged several related **auth callback** risks in `app/api/auth/callback/wtus-auth/route.ts` and `src/auth.ts`:

1. **Open redirect / cookie weakening via forwarded headers** ΓÇö when `APP_URL` is unset or localhost, `getAppBaseUrl()` can derive origin from `X-Forwarded-Host` / `X-Forwarded-Proto`, affecting post-login redirects and `Secure` / `__Secure-` cookie behavior.
2. **`checks: []` on the `wtus-auth` NextAuth provider** ΓÇö no built-in OAuth state/CSRF checks; defense relies entirely on the custom callback route.
3. **OAuth error logging** ΓÇö full error object logged on token exchange failure may include sensitive artifacts.

## Required changes

- In production, require `APP_URL` (non-localhost) and reject callbacks when derived base URL does not match configured `APP_URL`.
- Enable `checks: ['state']` on the `wtus-auth` provider for defense in depth, or document and test the custom-only path.
- Redact/sanitize OAuth error logs.
- Extend existing `auth-callback-redirect.test.ts` coverage for hostile forwarded headers in production mode.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Production cannot be tricked into redirecting users to attacker-controlled hosts after login.
- [ ] Session cookies always use intended `Secure` / `__Secure-` settings in production.
- [ ] OAuth logs do not emit tokens/secrets.
- [ ] Tests cover missing `APP_URL`, hostile forwarded headers, and state validation.

## Related issues

- #58 (trusted proxy / rate limits / cookie cleanup)

## Source

Automated deepsec scan (`unsafe-redirect`, `missing-csrf-state-check`, `secret-in-log`).

body:
## Summary

deepsec flagged a **CRITICAL** issue in `src/lib/oidc.ts`: the OIDC client secret resolves with fallbacks that can end as an empty string:

```ts
process.env.WTUS_DASHBOARD_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET?.trim() ||
process.env.AUTH_SECRET?.trim() ||
"";
```

If `WTUS_DASHBOARD_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` is unset in a deployment, the app may boot with a weak or empty OIDC client secret. That weakens token exchange and OIDC trust boundaries.

Related findings also noted `AUTH_SECRET` dual-use as an OIDC client secret fallback (`dual-use-secret`).

## Required changes

- Require `WTUS_DASHBOARD_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` at startup in non-local environments; fail fast if missing/blank.
- Remove the empty-string fallback and avoid reusing `AUTH_SECRET` as the OIDC client secret.
- Add startup validation/tests that production config rejects blank secrets.
- Document required env vars in deployment docs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] App refuses to start (or refuses OIDC login) when `WTUS_DASHBOARD_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` is missing in production.
- [ ] No code path uses `""` as an OIDC client secret.
- [ ] `AUTH_SECRET` is used only for session/signing concerns, not OIDC client auth.
- [ ] Tests cover missing-secret startup behavior.

## Source

Automated deepsec scan (`insecure-crypto`, `dual-use-secret`). 69 findings exported 2026-06-28.
title: [P0] Fail fast on missing OIDC client secret ΓÇö empty fallback in oidc.ts

## Problem
Weather-alert polling appends a new `WeatherAlertSource` record every time an existing alert is seen. There is no retention policy, resolution workflow, or protection against indefinite raw-payload growth.

## Required changes
- Define when a source observation is materially new versus a duplicate heartbeat.
- Update or aggregate repeated observations where appropriate.
- Mark alerts resolved/expired based on source semantics.
- Add retention for raw payloads and old source observations.
- Add indexes for unresolved-alert and source-event lookups.
- Report poll/source health separately from alert events.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Repeated unchanged polls do not create unbounded duplicate rows.
- [ ] Resolved alerts are marked and no longer dispatched as new.
- [ ] Retention is configurable and documented.
- [ ] Raw payload storage has size limits/redaction rules.
- [ ] Tests cover duplicate poll, changed alert, resolution, source outage, and cleanup.

## Relevant code
- `bot/plugins/weather-alerts/`
- `WeatherAlertEvent` and `WeatherAlertSource` models

## Problem
Recurring availability stores weekday and `HH:MM` strings without a timezone or materialization policy. One-time windows use timestamps. The UI and bot cannot reliably answer future availability across daylight-saving changes or members in different zones.

## Required work
- Select the organization/default timezone and whether members may override it.
- Define how recurring rules become queryable occurrence windows.
- Handle daylight-saving gaps/duplicates explicitly.
- Add overlap detection between recurring and one-time windows.
- Define edit/delete behavior for a rule versus one occurrence.
- Use the same availability service in web, bot, live events, and on-call features.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Timezone is stored/displayed explicitly.
- [ ] Queries for a date range return deterministic occurrences.
- [ ] DST transition tests pass.
- [ ] Overlaps and invalid ranges are handled consistently.
- [ ] Web and bot show the same current/upcoming availability.
- [ ] Documentation explains recurring schedule semantics.

## Related
Existing issue #1 covers the immediate future-date bug; this issue covers the underlying recurring/timezone model.

Alert dispatch combines all matching dispatch rules and applies every role mention to every target channel. A role intended for one channel can be pinged in another. `DiscordAlertChannel` section metadata is also ignored during dispatch.

- Apply only the rule mentions belonging to that destination.

- [ ] Section-specific rules do not leak into unrelated channels.

- [ ] Tests cover multiple channels, multiple rules, duplicate IDs, section filtering, and missing channels.

## Problem
Automatic brief delivery uses a process-local `Set` and a 15-minute interval. Restarts clear deduplication, multiple instances can duplicate sends, and there is no durable record of success or failure.

## Required changes
- Persist scheduled delivery attempts and idempotency keys.
- Define daily/weekly/event-only eligibility precisely.
- Claim due deliveries atomically so only one worker sends them.
- Record sent, skipped, failed, and retry states.
- Handle restarts and clock drift without duplicate sends.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Restarting the bot does not resend a completed brief.
- [ ] Two bot instances cannot send the same brief twice.
- [ ] Failed sends can retry with a bounded policy.
- [ ] Operators can inspect delivery status without reading raw logs.
- [ ] Tests cover restart, duplicate worker, failure, retry, weekly schedule, and no-work preference.

## Relevant code
- `bot/plugins/core/index.ts`
- `bot/core/scheduler.ts`
- Prisma schema/migration

## Problem
The app treats Leantime `editorId`/`userId` values as if they were local Prisma user IDs. They are different identity namespaces, so assignment filtering and bot briefs are unreliable.

## Required changes
- Add an explicit mapping between dashboard users and Leantime users.
- Provide an operator workflow to inspect and repair mappings.
- Reject assignments to unmapped users with an actionable error.
- Backfill mappings for current team members.
- Use the mapping in reads, writes, bot briefs, `/mytasks`, and portfolio generation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No code compares a Leantime user ID directly to a Prisma user ID.
- [ ] Mappings are unique and auditable.

The current Leantime adapter keeps partial Prisma metadata but has no reconciliation job or drift reporting. Remote updates can leave local section, assignment, due date, comment, and status metadata stale.

## Required changes

Task source-of-truth ADR, identity mapping, and unified task service.

Permission behavior is improvised per route and contradicts the product docs. Members can create tasks in any section, only global operators can update tasks, and `canWorkInSection()` is largely unused. Section leads do not have a coherent authority model.

## Deliverable
Create and implement one permission matrix covering resource/action pairs for:

- special requests and portfolios

- [ ] Tests include allowed and denied cases for every route method.

## Goal
Add a durable, Discord-first way to identify the current Nowcaster on call and manage handoffs.

## Required behavior
- Authorized users can set an on-call member, start time, end time, coverage area, and notes.
- Members can view the current and upcoming on-call assignment from Discord.
- The bot sends handoff reminders before a shift ends.

- On-call status should integrate with live-event assignments and availability rather than becoming an unrelated parallel scheduler.

- Define who may schedule or override on-call coverage.
- Define whether the existing recurring availability model can supply candidate windows.

- [ ] Handoffs and overrides are audited.
- [ ] Overlaps and invalid ranges are rejected.

- [ ] Bot restarts do not lose state or duplicate reminders.
- [ ] Tests cover scheduling, querying, overlap, handoff, expiry, timezone behavior, and authorization.

## Goal
Add a Discord-first workflow that records and shows which WTUS member currently controls the shared Agucero account. This must be an operational handoff record, not a free-form status message.

## Required behavior
- Provide a bot command for an authorized member to claim the account.
- Provide a command to release or hand off the account.
- Show the current holder, claim time, optional purpose, and expiration/expected release time.
- Prevent overlapping active claims unless an operator explicitly overrides them.
- Notify the previous holder and relevant operations channel on handoff or override.
- Persist the state in PostgreSQL so bot restarts do not erase it.
- Record an audit history of claims, releases, handoffs, and overrides.

## Authorization
Define which global or section roles may claim, release, inspect, and override the account. Enforce authorization server-side; do not rely only on Discord command visibility.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] State persists across bot and dashboard restarts.
- [ ] Only authorized WTUS members can mutate the state.
- [ ] There can be at most one active holder.
- [ ] A stale claim can expire automatically or be overridden with an audit entry.
- [ ] The bot clearly reports when nobody holds the account.
- [ ] Tests cover claim, duplicate claim, release, handoff, override, expiry, and unauthorized access.
- [ ] Operator documentation explains the workflow.

## Implementation note
Keep the primary interaction in Discord. A dashboard read-only status may be added only if useful; do not create another decorative dashboard card.

## Problem
The availability scheduler does not reliably allow a member to create a window on a future date. The UI performs extensive client-side date construction in `src/App.tsx`, while the API accepts loosely parsed date strings and silently falls back to the current time when parsing fails.

## Scope
- Reproduce the failure for tomorrow, later this week, next month, and across a month boundary.
- Define one timezone rule for entering, storing, and displaying availability.
- Fix client date construction so the selected calendar day is preserved.
- Make the API reject invalid or reversed windows instead of substituting `new Date()`.
- Ensure future one-time availability appears in the calendar and dashboard after refresh.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A member can schedule availability for any future day supported by the UI.
- [ ] Start and end times survive a page refresh without shifting dates.
- [ ] `endsAt` must be later than `startsAt`.
- [ ] Invalid date input returns HTTP 400 with a useful message.
- [ ] Behavior is correct in the production timezone and at daylight-saving boundaries.
- [ ] Automated tests cover same-day, future-day, month-boundary, invalid, and reversed ranges.

## Verification
1. Create windows for today, tomorrow, seven days out, and next month.
2. Refresh and confirm each window remains on the selected date.
3. Confirm the API rejects malformed and reversed dates.
4. Run the new API and browser tests.

## Relevant code
- `src/App.tsx` availability/calendar views
- `app/api/availability/route.ts`
- `app/api/availability/recurring/route.ts`
title: Cannot set schedule further than the current day
